name: LS-01 | Fun 002 | LinkedIn Event Registrations Sync
description:
# LS-01 | Fun 002 | LinkedIn Event Registrations Sync

**Ticket:** [Monday](https://brightdata-group.monday.com/boards/8667788707/pulses/12418264810)

## What it does
Runs per-event. For each event: fetches form + registrations, parses dynamically, stores in Postgres.

## Important logic
- **Dynamic parsing:** questionId varies between events! Map by `predefinedField`
  (FIRST_NAME/LAST_NAME/EMAIL/COMPANY_NAME/JOB_TITLE/COUNTRY)
- **Form fetch:** `leadForms/{form_id}` — form_id extracted from lead_gen_form via regex
- **Pagination:** stops when no elements / < 100. Dedup by id (LinkedIn returns duplicates)
- **Table:** `marketing.linkedin_registrations`, upsert ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING
  (DO NOTHING to avoid resetting hubspot_synced!)
- **Optimization:** event ended >2 days ago → registrations_synced = true (skipped next run)

## Fields vary between events
questionId is not stable — especially first/last name (and sometimes email).
That's why predefinedField mapping is required.

input.code:
# ---- inputs (both lists) ----
# input['leads']      => array of lead records (company, country, email, ...)
# input['list_items'] => array of { 'country' => '...', 'country_iso_code' => '...' }

leads = input['leads'] || []
rows  = input['list_items'] || []

# normalized list of blocked country names
blocked = rows.map { |r| r['country'].to_s.downcase.strip }.reject(&:empty?)

allowed_list = []
blocked_list = []

leads.each do |lead|
  c = lead['country'].to_s.downcase.strip

  # guard: keep South Sudan allowed even though "sudan" is blocked
  is_blocked =
    !c.include?('south sudan') &&
    blocked.any? { |name| c.include?(name) }

  if is_blocked
    hit = blocked.find { |name| c.include?(name) }
    iso = rows.find { |r| r['country'].to_s.downcase.strip == hit }&.dig('country_iso_code')
    blocked_list << lead.merge(
      "blocked_iso_code" => iso,
      "blocked_reason"   => "Forbidden country: #{lead['country']} (#{iso})"
    )
  else
    allowed_list << lead
  end
end

# ---- outputs (both lists) ----
{
  "allowed"       => allowed_list,
  "blocked"       => blocked_list,
  "allowed_count" => allowed_list.length,
  "blocked_count" => blocked_list.length
}
